KKR (NYSE:KKR) signed a definitive agreement to acquire Gen II Fund Services for $5.1 billion in enterprise value.

The deal acquires Gen II from private equity investors Hg and General Atlantic.

The transaction expands KKR fund administration capabilities across global private capital markets.

KKR (NYSE:KKR) agreed to acquire private capital fund administrator Gen II Fund Services for a total enterprise value of $5.1 billion.

The transaction represents a complete buyout from existing private equity investors Hg and General Atlantic.

"Gen II is exactly the type of financial services business we look for – a sophisticated sector leader with exceptional client relationships and a differentiated service model," said KKR Partner Chris Harrington.

Gen II currently provides administrative services to over 275 investment managers representing more than $2 trillion in assets.

Gen II quadrupled its revenue and EBITDA following a co-investment by General Atlantic and Hg in 2020.

The acquisition is subject to customary regulatory approvals and is expected to close in 2027.
